name: Photographer or creative freelancer
description: A photographer, videographer or other creative freelancer: services, a portfolio of projects, packages and clients' questions, with facts about the area served, delivery time, what clients receive, travel fees, the deposit and usage rights.

questions.question: Where do you take on work – which town or region, and do you travel further?
questions.help: For example "Brno and South Moravia, further by arrangement".

questions.question: How soon after the shoot do clients get their photos?
questions.help: For example "within 3 weeks; a preview of 20 photos within 3 days".

questions.question: What exactly do clients receive?
questions.help: For example "edited photos in full resolution in an online gallery to download", or the approximate number per hour.

questions.question: Do you charge for travel? How?
questions.help: For example "free within 30 km, then 0.30 EUR per km" or "none".

questions.question: Do you ask for a deposit to reserve a date? How much, and what happens if the client cancels?
questions.help: Write it as your contract says it. Leave it empty if you take no deposit.

questions.question: How may clients use the photos, and may you show them in your portfolio?
questions.help: For example "private use without limits; commercial use by agreement". Copyright and image rights differ by country – check your terms.

questions.question: Since which year have you been working professionally?

audit.message: Add at least three projects to the portfolio – clients book a photographer by their work.
Add your packages with the hours, number of photos and price – clients compare them before they enquire.
Say how soon clients get their photos – it is one of the first questions.
Say how clients may use the photos – it avoids disputes later.
Publish a privacy policy page – photos of people and enquiries are personal data; check what your law requires.

claude: A photographer's site sells with images: the portfolio leads, the photos are large and the words few – who you photograph, in what style, where, and how to book. The references collection is the portfolio, one item per shoot or project; the plans collection holds the packages with the same wording (hours, number of photos, delivery) across them. Use only the owner's own photos, never stock images, and publish people – above all children – only when the owner confirms they agreed. Never invent clients, testimonials, awards, publications, prices or years of experience. Delivery time, travel fee, deposit and usage rights are facts, stated as in the owner's contract; copyright and image rights differ by country, so say they should be checked rather than stating the law. Every image needs alt text describing what it shows.
